articles.text: Jean warns Bob not to make plans for Sunday because she wants to go to the bullfight again. Bob asks why and Jean explains they promised to take the children to the countryside. Bob suggests sending the children with the maid; Jean refuses, saying the children want to be with their parents.

Jean and Bob argue about bullfighting. Jean says bullfighting is horrible and cruel and recalls nearly fainting during the last corrida. Bob finds it exciting and says the last bullfight was phenomenal. He thinks Jean reacted that way because it was her first bullfight; Jean replies that she doesn’t want to see any more.

Jean and Bob want to go to the horse races. Jean worries about who will watch the children; Bob suggests leaving them with the maid, but Jean says the maid wants to go out. Bob replies that she can go out tomorrow instead.
